speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and if they are itchy or painful? Also, have you noticed any fever or other symptoms recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have the lesions changed in appearance, such as developing a central depression or umbilication, and have you noticed any spread to other parts of the body like the face or extremities? I will also inspect the lesions closely for any signs of inflammation or secondary infection.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of pearly papules with central umbilication and the recent exposure in daycare strongly suggests Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
